verses.text: Paul came to Derbe and then Lystra. A disciple named Timothy was there. His mother was a Jewish believer, and his father was Greek.
The believers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of Timothy.
Paul wanted Timothy to travel with him, so he circumcised him because of the Jews in that area, who all knew his father was Greek.
As they traveled through the cities, they passed on the decisions the apostles and elders in Jerusalem had made for the believers to follow.
So the churches grew stronger in the faith and increased in number every day.
They traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia because the Holy Spirit stopped them from speaking the word in Asia.
When they reached the border of Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus wouldn’t let them.
So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
During the night Paul saw a vision: a man from Macedonia was standing there, begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
After Paul saw the vision, we immediately prepared to leave for Macedonia. We concluded that God had called us to announce the Good News to them.
We sailed from Troas and went straight to Samothrace. The next day we reached Neapolis,
and from there Philippi, a leading city in that part of Macedonia and a Roman colony. We stayed in the city for several days.
On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the riverside, where we thought there might be a place of prayer. We sat down and spoke with the women who had gathered there.
One of them was Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from Thyatira who worshiped God. As she listened to Paul, the Lord opened her heart to receive his message.
After Lydia and her household were baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a faithful believer in the Lord, come stay at my home.” She persuaded us to go.
One day as we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl with a fortune-telling spirit met us. Her predictions made a lot of money for her owners.
She followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men serve the Most High God and are telling you how to be saved!”
She kept doing this for many days. Finally Paul, very annoyed, turned to the spirit and said, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I command you to come out of her!” The spirit came out at once.
When her owners realized their chance to make money was gone, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the city officials.
They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and they’re stirring up our city.
“They’re promoting customs that we Romans aren’t allowed to accept or practice.”
The crowd joined in against Paul and Silas. The magistrates ordered their clothes torn off and commanded that they be beaten with rods.
After they had beaten them severely, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them carefully.
The jailer followed the order, put them in the inner cell, and secured their feet in stocks.
Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God while the other prisoners listened.
Suddenly a powerful earthquake shook the prison foundations. All the doors flew open, and everyone’s chains came loose.
The jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open. Thinking the prisoners had escaped, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself.
But Paul shouted, “Don’t hurt yourself! We’re all here!”
The jailer called for lights, rushed in, and trembling, fell down in front of Paul and Silas.
Then he brought them outside and asked, “Sirs, what do I need to do to be saved?”
They answered, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household.”
Then they shared the Lord’s message with him and everyone in his home.
At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. Then he and everyone in his household were baptized right away.
He brought them into his home and served them a meal. He and his whole household were filled with joy because they had come to believe in God.
When morning came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order, “Release those men.”
The jailer told Paul, “The magistrates have ordered you released. You can leave now and go in peace.”

But Paul told the officers, “They beat us in public without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us in prison. And now they want to send us away quietly? No. Let them come themselves and escort us out.”
The officers reported this to the magistrates. When they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they became afraid.
They came and apologized to them. Then they escorted them out and asked them to leave the city.
After leaving the prison, Paul and Silas went to Lydia’s home. They met with the believers there, encouraged them, and then left.
